WebSocket upgrade that gives a person control of one of the session's agent tabs without a takeover ticket (the browser sheet). Requires steer, a person_device token or the local socket (agent_client tokens and MCP socket clients get 403 person_device_required), and an Origin matching the Host; the bearer subprotocol works as on the takeover stream. The daemon streams TakeoverServerMessage frames and `page` updates and accepts TakeoverInput, including navigate/back/forward/reload/close_tab. One controller per tab (409 control_in_use); a pending takeover ticket on the tab returns 409 takeover_active; private sessions return 409 private_session. The control ends when the client closes the socket, after 300 s without accepted input (ended idle), on token revocation (ended revoked) or when the tab is gone (ended tab_unavailable); the agent then regains the tab with its earlier snapshots and references voided. Opening, navigation, tab closing and the end of control are written to the audit log; typed text is not.

get.description: Whether this caller can dictate right now. A caller that POST would refuse (agent clients: MCP/CLI agent tokens and marked socket clients) gets available false with reason person_device_required, without any transcriber lookup. Otherwise available is true when channels.stt_cmd is set or the openai account pool holds a first-party OpenAI API key (ChatGPT-plan sign-ins, relays and plugin accounts are never used), and false with reason stt_unavailable when neither is; nothing leaves the computer to answer. max_bytes is the largest decoded clip (8 MiB, or channels.max_audio_bytes when smaller); max_seconds is the longest clip a client should record (120).

post.description: Transcribe one recorded clip (base64) for the person's composer. channels.stt_cmd runs locally first with the clip in a private temporary file that is deleted when the command ends; otherwise the clip goes to OpenAI's transcription API (gpt-4o-mini-transcribe) with the first usable OpenAI API key of the openai account pool. language only reaches OpenAI, as its primary subtag. The clip and the text are never stored, logged or added to a chat. At most two clips are transcribed at once and four more wait for a slot; beyond that the request is refused with 429 stt_busy before its clip is decoded. The request body may be at most the base64 size of max_bytes plus 64 KiB and must arrive within 30 seconds.

400.description: A body that is not a TranscribeRequest, bad base64, an empty clip, a mime that is not audio/*, or a language that is not a short BCP-47 tag

403.description: Only the person's own device or the local socket dictates; agent clients (MCP/CLI agent tokens and marked socket clients) are refused

408.description: The request body did not arrive within 30 seconds; its place is freed for others

409.description: No transcriber: set channels.stt_cmd or add an OpenAI API key

413.description: The clip is larger than max_bytes from GET /v1/stt, or the body is larger than its base64 size plus 64 KiB

429.description: Two clips are being transcribed and four more are waiting; try again shortly

502.description: The transcriber failed or timed out; its output is never returned

get.description: WebSocket upgrade for a pending takeover ticket whose target has a tab_id. The daemon streams JPEG frames of that tab (TakeoverServerMessage, JSON text) and forwards TakeoverInput messages to that tab only, with coordinates in viewport CSS pixels. One controller per ticket (409 takeover_in_use); an Origin header must match the Host. Browsers, which cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket, send the token as `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: openside.v1, openside.bearer.<token>`; the daemon answers with `openside.v1` only. The stream ends with an `ended` message on done/reject/expiry, idle timeout, token revocation or tab loss. While the ticket is pending, agent browser tools on the tab are refused with takeover_active.

post.description: Delete every saved sign-in, authenticator and passkey; model keys, channel and MCP secrets stay. Same gate and codes as export (local socket, `confirm: true`, fresh authentication). Audited (`clear`: `allowed`, then `cleared` with the count; refusals `denied`). 500 vault_cleared_audit_incomplete (cleared).

Every saved sign-in and authenticator as CSV (`name,url,username,password,otpauth`, one row per allowed origin; passkeys cannot be exported and are counted in `skipped`; model keys, channel and MCP secrets are never included). Local socket only, `confirm: true`, and fresh authentication: the passphrase in the body (passphrase vaults), `biometric: true`, or a person's unlock in the last 5 minutes; a keyring vault without biometric unlock needs only the confirmation. Wrong passphrases are throttled like unlock. Refusals are audited (`export`: `denied`); an export is audited `allowed`, then `exported`. Served with Cache-Control: no-store. 400 confirmation_required, wrong_passphrase, passphrase_not_used; 403 local_access_required, biometric_failed; 409 vault_unavailable, reauth_required, biometric_unavailable; 429 too_many_attempts; 500 audit_unavailable.

post.description: Drop the decrypted vault from daemon memory; vault tools stop working until it is unlocked again. Audited (`lock`) after locking, attributed to the caller; 500 vault_locked_audit_incomplete means it is locked but unrecorded. Open a locked vault with its recovery key and give it a new unlock key: `passphrase` (8+ characters) for a passphrase vault, the OS keyring's key (created when missing) for a keyring vault. The saved recovery key keeps working. Local socket only; wrong keys are throttled like passphrases. Audited (`recover`: `recovered`, `denied` with wrong_recovery_key, or `failed` with the code). 400 passphrase_required, passphrase_not_used, weak_passphrase; 403 local_access_required, wrong_recovery_key; 409 vault_already_unlocked, vault_not_set_up, recovery_not_configured; 429 too_many_attempts; 503 vault_unsupported, keyring_unavailable; 500 vault_recovered_audit_incomplete (recovered).

Generate a recovery key and return it once; any earlier key stops working. It is stored nowhere: only the vault key sealed with it is kept next to the vault file, and it is masked in later output. Same gate and codes as export (local socket, `confirm: true`, fresh authentication). Audited (`recovery_key`: `allowed`, then `generated`, both before the old key is replaced). Served with Cache-Control: no-store.

get.description: Password settings: auto-lock idle time, biometric unlock (with whether this computer supports it), autofill rules, default access policy, the fixed incognito exclusion and recovery-key state. Never values.

patch.description: Change password settings; absent fields keep their value. Saved to the config file and applied at once; every change is audited (`settings_update`, with the changed key names only). Tightening is open to every vault caller; loosening (longer auto-lock, biometric unlock off, autofill or auto-submit on, insecure pages allowed, fewer excluded domains, a less strict default policy) needs the local socket or a person's device. Turning biometric unlock on needs the local socket, a keyring vault and a passing biometric check. 400 invalid_value, invalid_domain, incognito_always_disabled; 403 local_access_required, person_access_required, biometric_failed; 409 biometric_unavailable; 500 settings_saved_audit_incomplete (saved).

post.description: Create the vault file. Keyring backends take no body passphrase and keep a random wrapping key in the OS keyring; a passphrase vault needs `passphrase` (8+ characters), which is never stored or returned. With biometric unlock on, a keyring vault is created only from the local socket with `biometric: true` and a passing check. Every attempt that reaches the vault is audited (`setup`: `completed` or `failed` with the code), attributed to the caller (`device:<id>` or `local`). 400 passphrase_required, passphrase_not_used, weak_passphrase; 403 biometric_required, biometric_failed; 409 vault_already_set_up; 500 vault_set_up_audit_incomplete (set up and unlocked); 503 keyring_unavailable, vault_unsupported.

Decrypt the vault: a keyring vault re-reads its key from the OS keyring; a passphrase vault needs `passphrase`. Already unlocked is a no-op. Audited (`unlock`: `unlocked`, `denied` with wrong_passphrase, or `failed` with the code), attributed to the caller; an unlock whose record cannot be written does not happen (500 audit_unavailable). Each caller gets 5 wrong passphrases, then waits 30 s, doubling per further wrong one up to 15 min; a success resets it. Paired devices together get 20 wrong passphrases per 15 minutes; the Unix socket is exempt from that shared limit. At most one attempt per caller, and two across paired devices, run at once. Throttled attempts get 429 too_many_attempts with `Retry-After` seconds, before any key derivation, and are not audited. 400 passphrase_required, passphrase_not_used, wrong_passphrase; 409 vault_not_set_up; 503 keyring_unavailable, vault_unsupported.

429.description: Too many wrong passphrases; retry after the `Retry-After` header's seconds
